title: Which script produces this output?
examObjective: Defining, using, and reusing DataWeave modules, functions, and variables
prompt:
Every node has a value `v` and may have `kids`. Add up every `v` at every depth. Given the payload below,

**which script produces exactly this output?**

```
10
```

options:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
fun sumTree(t) = t.v + sum((t.kids default []) map sumTree($))
---
sumTree(payload)

%dw 2.0
output application/json
fun sumTree(t) = sum((t.kids default []) map sumTree($))
---
sumTree(payload)

%dw 2.0
output application/json
fun sumTree(t) = t.v + sum((t.kids default []).v)
---
sumTree(payload)

solution:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
fun sumTree(t) = t.v + sum((t.kids default []) map sumTree($))
---
sumTree(payload)

explanation.approach: A tree of unknown depth needs a function that calls itself on each child. It also needs a base case: a node with no `kids` must still return its own value, which is what `default []` makes possible.

snippets.script:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
fun sumTree(t) = t.v + sum((t.kids default []) map sumTree($))
---
sumTree(payload)

snippets.note: Every leaf returns the sum of no children, which is 0.
